title: Human-in-the-Loop Automation with n8n — Liam McGarrigle
talk_summary: A hands-on n8n workshop building a Gmail/Calendar agent, focused on adding a human-in-the-loop approval gate in front of destructive tool calls and on making agent behavior inspectable via per-node execution logs.

takeaways.technique: Interception-layer human approval gate on destructive tools
takeaways.what_they_do: Insert a human-review node on the tool branch so the agent cannot invoke a destructive tool (send email, create event) without an explicit approve/deny; the agent is unaware the gate exists and just sees the tool call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it just cannot get past this layer. It can't use this tool without going through this chat

takeaways.technique: Per-field tool schemas instead of blanket API access
takeaways.what_they_do: Each tool exposes individual fields the model may set; unset fields are locked, so the agent can only write the parameters you explicitly enable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it has every single field individually. So it can only set the things that we tell it to specifically

takeaways.technique: Tool descriptions as the primary steering surface
takeaways.what_they_do: Node name = tool name, node description = tool description passed to the LLM on every call; they put tool-specific instructions in the description rather than the system prompt, and add per-field descriptions to disambiguate confusing params.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The node name is the tool name. The node description is the tool description. So you can actually put in full prompts here

takeaways.technique: Sub-agent decomposition to control context and per-agent model choice
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of piling all tools on one agent, build specialized sub-agents (email/calendar, GitHub issues, etc.) and have a main agent call them; each sub-agent can use a different LLM optimized for its task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: That way you're not adding so much context to just the main agent and you can change the model between each one

takeaways.technique: Execution trace inspection per node/tool call
takeaways.what_they_do: Every run shows which tools were called, the exact inputs/outputs per node, and full logs; you can copy a past execution into the editor to debug with real data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can see exactly what tools it used... we can see the exact output from that... detailed logs of everything that happened

takeaways.technique: Scheduled background runs with human-gated outputs
takeaways.what_they_do: Add a schedule trigger so the agent runs hourly on a task (e.g. clear inbox, scan PRs) and pushes proposed actions to a channel for human approval rather than acting autonomously.
takeaways.evidence_quote: imagine if we just added a schedule trigger, and had that run every hour... it's still human in the looping for everything but just running in the background
